newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga sets up a Child Protection Authority and orders islandwide crackdown on paedophiles.
Navy kills at least 30 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas during attacks on rebel boats in last 10 days.
Pure Beverages Company, bottlers of Coca Cola, seeks duty waiver to import Coke after one-month long strike at bottling plant depletes stocks.
Commonwealth of Independent States was number one buyer of Sri Lanka tea last year, having pruchased 46.6 million kg.
Peace conference held in eastern Batticaloa district to calm ethnic tension between Tamils and Moslems. Tension was high after Moslem civilian homeguard was killed by suspected Tamil guerrillas.
Two policemen wounded after suspected Tamil guerrillas threw grenade at a government office in northern frontline town of Vavuniya on Sunday night.
Cyprus-registered cargo vessel, believed to have carried arms for the LTTE, attacked and detained at the eastern Trincomalee harbour by military.
Wednesday is last day to hand in nominations for next month's local government elections. Deadline is 12 noon.
Army commander Lt. General Rohan Daluwatte inspects areas freshly captured by troops on offensive in the northern Vanni region.
Military launches investigation on suspected arms ship for rebels. Grills ship's Cuban crew.
